cor.heading: Net sales and Cost of sales
cor.text: Net sales for the three months ended June 30, 2026 totaled $940 million, an increase of $50 million, or 6%, compared to the three months ended June 30, 2025. Cost of sales and cost of sales as a percentage of net sales were $724 million and 77%, respectively, during the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $693 million and 78%, respectively, during the three months ended June 30, 2025. The change in net sales, cost of sales, and gross profit for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was primarily driven by the impacts below.

oi.heading: Other operating income, net
oi.text: Other operating income, net was de minimis compared to income of $6 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025. The change in other operating income, net was primarily driven by a decrease in separation-related benefits. Other operating income, net was comprised of the following:

sga.heading: Selling, general and administrative expenses (SG&A)
sga.text: SG&A for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $128 million as compared to $112 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. SG&A as a percentage of net sales was 14% for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to 13% for the three months ended June 30, 2025. SG&A expenses increased period-over-period, primarily attributable to increased employee costs, including stock-based compensation, as well as foreign currency exchange impacts and professional fees.

other_opex.heading: Other operating income, net
other_opex.text: Other operating income, net was de minimis compared to income of $6 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025. nonop.heading: Interest expense
nonop.text: Interest expense was $21 million in the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025.

tax.heading: Provision for income taxes
tax.text:
Provision for income taxes was $27 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, resulting in an effective tax rate of 40%. This is compared to $29 million, or 39%, for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The effective tax rates for the respective periods were comparable to one another.

For further details, see Note 7, “Income Taxes,” to the Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements for the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities was $144 million and $97 million in the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The increase in cash from operating activities for the six months ended June 30, 2026 compared with the six months ended June 30, 2025 was primarily due to strong execution of inventory optimization initiatives and working capital discipline.

capex.text: Net cash used in investing activities was $53 million and $68 million in the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively, related to timing of capital expenditures. As a percentage of sales, capital expenditures were 3.0% and 4.1% for the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

Fuel Systems.text: PHINIA is a diversified industrial supplier and global leader in the development of fuel systems, electrical systems, and aftermarket solutions, with a strong portfolio of trusted brands that includes DELPHI®, DELCO REMY®, and HARTRIDGE™. With over 100 years of manufacturing expertise and industry relationships, PHINIA has approximately 12,500 talented employees and over 40 locations in 20 countries and is headquartered in Auburn Hills, Michigan, USA. PHINIA systems and solutions are designed to keep combustion engines operating at peak performance across a variety of applications: medium- and heavy-duty commercial vehicle (on-road vehicles used for commercial transport classified class 4–8, 14,001 pounds or heavier); light commercial vehicle (on-road vehicles used for commercial transport classified class 1–3, 14,000 pounds or lighter); light passenger vehicles (on-road vehicles used primarily for carrying passengers); and off-highway, industrial, and other (including construction and agricultural machinery, vocational vehicles, marine, industrial applications, power generation, and aerospace and defense). PHINIA’s service solutions include vehicle repair and replacement parts, offering both new and remanufactured products through the original equipment manufacturer dealer network and the independent aftermarket channel.

PHINIA’s service solutions include vehicle repair and replacement parts, offering both new and remanufactured products through the original equipment manufacturer dealer network and the independent aftermarket channel.

Power Systems.text: The Company’s business is comprised of two reportable segments: Power Systems and Aftermarket Solutions.

Aftermarket Solutions.text: PHINIA is a diversified industrial supplier and global leader in the development of fuel systems, electrical systems, and aftermarket solutions, with a strong portfolio of trusted brands that includes DELPHI®, DELCO REMY®, HARTRIDGE™ and stoba®. With over 100 years of manufacturing expertise and industry relationships, PHINIA has approximately 13,500 talented employees and over 40 locations in 21 countries and is headquartered in Auburn Hills, Michigan, USA. Our systems and solutions are designed to keep combustion engines operating at peak performance across a variety of applications: medium- and heavy-duty commercial vehicle (on-road vehicles used for commercial transport classified as class 4-8, 14,001 pounds or heavier), light commercial vehicle (on-road vehicles used for commercial transport classified as class 1-3, 14,000 pounds or lighter), light passenger vehicle (on-road vehicles used primarily for carrying passengers), and off-highway, industrial, and other (including construction and agricultural machinery, vocational vehicles, marine, industrial applications, power generation, and aerospace and defense). PHINIA’s service solutions include vehicle repair and replacement parts, offering both new and remanufactured products through the original equipment manufacturer dealer network and the independent aftermarket channel.

intro.text: PHINIA Inc. (together with its consolidated subsidiaries, the Company or PHINIA) is a Delaware corporation incorporated in 2023. The Company is a leader in the development, design and manufacture of integrated components and systems that are designed to optimize performance, increase efficiency and reduce emissions in combustion and hybrid propulsion for commercial vehicles and industrial applications (medium-duty and heavy-duty trucks, buses and other off-highway construction, marine, agricultural and aerospace and defense), light commercial vehicles (vans and trucks) and light passenger vehicles (passenger cars, mini-vans, cross-overs and sport-utility vehicles). We are a global supplier to most major original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) seeking to meet and exceed increasingly stringent global regulatory requirements and satisfy consumer demands for an enhanced user experience.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
